#+title: Test fixtures

Pull requests as GitHub serves them, for tests and for
=approve-dev-offline-mode=.  No test touches the network
([[file:../../docs/decisions.org::*D19 Tests: buttercup, undercover, fixtures, no network][D19]]); the tests answer Approve's requests from these files instead.

* Scenarios
One scenario is one JSON file, =<name>.json=: one pull request, and every
request that loads it with GitHub's response.

#+begin_src json
{
  "approveFixture": 1,
  "name": "medium",
  "description": "What the scenario is for",
  "pullRequest": {
    "host": "github.com",
    "owner": "acme-example",
    "repo": "rocket",
    "number": 202,
    "viewer": "vera-example"
  },
  "exchanges": [
    {
      "request": {
        "kind": "graphql",
        "name": "queries/pull-request-files.graphql",
        "variables": {"owner": "acme-example", "name": "rocket", "number": 202}
      },
      "response": {
        "status": 200,
        "headers": {"X-RateLimit-Remaining": "4998"},
        "body": {"data": {"repository": {"pullRequest": {"...": "..."}}}}
      }
    },
    {
      "request": {
        "kind": "rest",
        "method": "GET",
        "resource": "/repos/acme-example/rocket/pulls/202/files",
        "params": {"per_page": 100, "page": 1}
      },
      "response": {"status": 200, "headers": {"Link": "..."}, "body": ["..."]}
    }
  ]
}
#+end_src

- =approveFixture= :: the format version (=approve-dev-fixture-format=).
- =pullRequest= :: the pull request (web host, owner, repository, number)
  and the login of the viewer the responses were made for.  Tests give it
  to =approve-model-init= (=approve-dev-scenario-meta=).
- =request= :: what identifies a request (=approve-dev-request-key=).
  GraphQL: the query file under =graphql/= and its variables; a later
  page adds =after=.  REST: method, resource and parameters.  Variables
  and parameters match in any order, and numbers match their strings.
- =response= :: the HTTP status, the headers that matter (rate limit,
  =Link=, =Retry-After=; nothing else is kept) and the body, the whole
  JSON document as GitHub sends it: for GraphQL that is ={"data": …}=.

A body reads back as ghub decodes it (=json-parse-buffer= with
=:object-type alist :array-type list :null-object nil :false-object nil=):
objects are alists with symbol keys, arrays are lists, and =null=,
=false= and =[]= are all nil.  A status outside 200–299 is replayed as
that failure.

* Reading and replaying
- =(approve-dev-read-scenario "medium")= :: the scenario as a plist
  (=:owner=, =:repo=, =:number=, =:viewer=, =:exchanges=, …).
- =(approve-dev-make-replay-transport SCENARIOS LATENCY)= :: a function to
  put in =approve-api-transport=.  It answers each request from the
  matching exchange on a timer, and fails one it has no exchange for
  with a 404 that says which request it was (also in =*approve-log*=).
- =M-x approve-dev-offline-mode= :: replays every scenario in this
  directory; the request's owner, name and number pick the scenario.

* Recording
=M-x approve-dev-record= asks for a pull request URL and a scenario name.
It runs the loading plan (the six queries in =graphql/queries/= with all
pages, except the checks query's first page only, and the REST files list
with all pages) through the installed transport, records every exchange,
and writes =<name>.json= here.  Recordings keep no tokens or
Authorization headers.  People's logins, names and emails become stable
fakes (=user-1=, =Person 2=, …) unless the command gets a prefix argument;
mentions inside comment text are not changed, so read a recording before
committing it.
